ui.optionalDesc: Choose your deity's domain at level 1
ui.subclassDesc: Chosen at level 1. Your Divine Domain shapes your spellcasting and subclass features.
ui.featDesc: Clerics get 5 ASI slots (levels 4, 8, 12, 16, 19). Origin Feats come from your Background; General Feats fill ASI slots.
ui.backgroundNote: In 2024 D&D, your Background sets ability scores (+2/+1 or +1/+1/+1) and grants an Origin Feat. Wisdom is non-negotiable.
ui.multiclassNote: Brief dips for specific features. Don't invest more levels than the feature requires.
ui.weaponNote: Focus on simple weapons. Clerics get Weapon Mastery at level 1.
ui.armorNote: Clerics are proficient in light, medium, and shields.

subclasses.name: Life Domain
subclasses.d: The ultimate healer and buffer. Disciple of Life makes your healing spells significantly more powerful. Perfect for parties that need reliable healing.

subclasses.name: Light Domain
subclasses.d: Excellent damage output combined with strong utility. Flame Strike and Scorching Ray are fantastic damage spells. Guiding Bolt is the best first-level spell for rogues.

subclasses.name: War Domain
subclasses.d: The best martial Cleric subclass. War Priest gives extra attacks, and Battle Magic allows spellcasting with a weapon and shield. Great for frontline support.

subclasses.name: Trickery Domain
subclasses.d: Focuses on deception and misdirection. Blessing of Luck and Invoke Duplicity provide unique tactical options. Less optimal but flavorful.

species.d: An additional skill and an Origin Feat on top of your Background's feat. Essential for Wisdom-based builds.
Lucky provides crucial insurance on key saves. Brave helps with concentration. Perfect for any Wisdom-based build.
Gnomish Cunning grants Advantage on Int/Wis/Cha saves vs. magic. Excellent for concentration checks.
Hellish Rebuke is a nice reaction and Darkvision is always welcome. Infernal Legacy provides utility.
Dwarven Resilience (poison resistance and advantage on saves) is genuinely good for a frontline Cleric.
Darkvision, Keen Senses (Perception), and immunity to sleep effects. Wood Elves get extra speed.
Two extra skills and perpetual Advantage on Charisma checks. Good for a Face Cleric build.
Psychic resistance is useful, but the rest is very campaign-dependent. Good if the DM uses a lot of mind-affecting magic.
Breath Weapon and elemental resistances are fine features, but nothing here is specifically useful to the Cleric.
Giant's Power adds Str-based options that you won't use, and Stone's Endurance competes with your Bonus Action.
Adrenaline Rush gives extra mobility on a Bonus Action, which competes with Channel Divinity. Relentless Endurance is solid insurance.
Shifting provides a burst of survivability, but you'd rather use your Bonus Action for healing or spells.

abilityNotes.n: Dump stat. Nothing a typical Cleric does uses Strength.
Not crucial, but helpful for initiative and AC if wearing light armor.
Hit points and concentration checks are always important, especially for frontline Clerics.
Dump stat. Only needed for Arcana if you want it.
Your primary ability. Spells, spell save DC, spell attack bonus, and your best save. Your Background must increase this.
Helpful for Persuasion and Intimidation if you're playing a Face. Not essential but useful.

skills.d: Useful for a Nature-themed Cleric or if your party lacks animal handling.
Functionally useless. You should never be grappling.
Essential for a Face or support Cleric. Helps read people and anticipate intentions.
Helpful but not as important as Perception or Insight.
The core Cleric skill. Crucial for stabilizing allies and providing healing outside combat.
Useful for a Nature-themed Cleric or if your party lacks nature knowledge.
Most important skill in the game after Insight. Several party members should have it.
Helpful for a Knowledge-focused Cleric or if your party lacks religious knowledge.
Situational. Some domains (like Trickery) make this more useful.
Useful for a Nature-themed Cleric or if your party lacks survival skills.

backgrounds.d: Excellent ability scores and skills. Religious background fits the Cleric perfectly. (PHB)
Absolutely fantastic for the Cleric — especially for a Trickery Domain or Face build. (PHB)
Perfect for a stealthy or underworld-connected Cleric. (PHB)
Good ability scores and Musician is welcome in any party. (PHB)
Good ability scores and skills for a scholarly or artisan Cleric. (PHB)
Excellent ability scores and access to Medicine and Religion. Perfect for a scholarly or reclusive Cleric. (PHB)
Perfect for a leadership-focused Cleric. Good stats, skills, and access to Influence. (PHB)
Good ability scores and good skills for a maritime-themed Cleric. (PHB)
Good ability scores and good skills for a war-themed Cleric. (PHB)
Good ability scores, good skills, and Lucky. (PHB)
Bad ability scores. If you want Alert, look at Inquisitive. (PHB)
Good ability scores and skills for a Cha-investing Cleric. (FRHoF)

feats.d: The best general-purpose healing feat. Battle Medic can be used as a Bonus Action with Fast Hands (Thief Rogue) or with features that grant Bonus Actions.
An easy choice on any character. Three extra d20 rolls per long rest on attacks, checks, or saves.
Standard builds can use buffs like Guidance or Mage Armor. Good for utility spells.
A great way to contribute to any party.
Clerics get fewer skills than Rogues, but a small party may still need more coverage.
Never a bad choice. Helps with initiative, which is important for healing and buffing.
Timely Retreat is really good. (ABoH)
Heroic Inspiration is always useful. A great choice on literally any character. (ABoH)
1d6 damage isn't worth Concentration, but Hex's debuff on Wisdom ability checks helps you stay hidden. (LFL)
Neat but not especially impactful. Crafting mundane gear stops mattering early.
Faerie Fire may help, but you already have easy Advantage from your spells. (LFL)
The Help Action isn't useful enough to justify this unless you're a Hobgoblin. (FRHoF)
Your weapon damage die isn't a big enough part of your output to make this impactful.
You should literally never make an unarmed strike.
If you need this, you need to be using your class features more to stay safely out of reach.
Not as useful for Clerics since most healing spells don't require two weapons.
This feat was made for the Rogue. Less useful for Clerics who can heal themselves.
A climb speed is the next best thing to flight. Standing up quickly from prone helps in combat.
Helpful for spellcasting. Misty Step may be redundant with your spells, but more spells add real utility.
A massive amount of temporary hit points. Wait until you have 20 Wisdom first since it can't improve Wisdom.
Never a bad choice. Hard to pick the right ability until you have 20 Wisdom and all the feats you want.
Potentially an easy way to protect allies via Opportunity Attacks.
You're almost certainly going to learn Invisibility. Free castings are a reliable bonus.
Too situational on its own, though it nicely complements infiltration.
Won't contribute meaningfully to Cleric capabilities, but THP snacks are always welcome.
Even for a Knowledge Cleric, this is hard to justify.
Great insurance against spellcasters, but hiding keeps you untargetable.
Competes too much with crucial class features and action economy.
Rogues get very few slashing weapons, but this can work with whips.
Too situational.
Too situational.
Very useful for concentration checks. One of the best feats for spellcasters.
Not worth the feat. Use your spells for damage instead.
Clerics' weapons almost all deal Bludgeoning. Crusher needs bludgeoning and doesn't give a Wisdom increase.
Bad and conflicts with your crucial Bonus Action class features.
Clerics should not be grappling.
The ability score increase is useless and you'll only get the damage bonus once per round.
Clerics already get heavy armor proficiency. This feat is redundant.
Not worth the feat. Put +2 into Wisdom and wear light armor if you want stealth.
You should not be using a polearm to attack unless you're a War Cleric.
Useful for ritual spells, but not essential.
Clerics get proficiency with shields. This feat adds some utility but isn't essential.
You have your spells for movement.
You cannot use Sneak Attack with spell attacks (that's a Rogue feature).
You already get Weapon Mastery slots from your class.

epicBoons.d: Stunningly powerful combined with Reliable Talent. Every proficient skill becomes extraordinary.
Great on a frontline Cleric where you draw many attacks.
Last Stand is great insurance for any character.
Excellent for a stealthy Cleric. Note that Hide, Search, and Study are Actions that break the invisibility.
Probably your only built-in option for handling invisible enemies at high levels.
Extra movement is nice, but you can already use your spells for movement.
More useful to support allies' save-or-suck spells than for anything you're doing.
You don't attack frequently enough for the damage boost to be meaningful. Magic weapon handles resistance.
Functionally removes your ability to miss. If you used two-weapon fighting for a second attack chance, you can safely stop.
Immunity to poison is great, but not essential for most Cleric builds.
Great insurance for any character, but not essential.

classFeatures.d: Your core feature. Wisdom is your spellcasting ability. You prepare spells each day.
Choose your deity's domain. This shapes your spellcasting and grants domain-specific features.
New in 2024. Clerics get 2 slots. Vex grants Advantage (qualifies for Sneak Attack); Nick enables a bonus attack for a second d20 roll.
Channel divine energy to channel positive or negative energy. Life Domain heals, Death Domain damages.
Force undead to flee. Essential for undead encounters.
Your domain grants a powerful feature. Life Domain gets Disciple of Life for healing.
Destroy undead of increasing CR. Essential for undead encounters.
You can use Channel Divinity twice per short or long rest.
Increase a ability score or gain a feat.
Your domain grants another powerful feature. Life Domain gets Blessed Healer.
You can use a holy symbol as a spellcasting focus.
Increase a ability score or gain a feat.
You can use Channel Divinity three times per short or long rest.
Increase a ability score or gain a feat.
Your domain grants a final powerful feature.
Maximize all healing dice on your spells. Huge boost to your healing output.
Increase a ability score or gain a feat.
Your domain feature becomes even more powerful.

optional.d: Add your Wisdom modifier to any healing spell of 1st level or higher. Makes your healing significantly more powerful.
You gain temporary hit points when you heal others. Perfect for a frontline healer.

optional.n: Light Domain: Radiance of the Dawn
optional.d: Add radiant damage to your spells and turn undead. Excellent damage output.
Add your Wisdom modifier to damage of your light or fire spells. Great for damage output.
Bonus Action attacks. Perfect for a martial Cleric.
Add radiant damage to your weapon attacks. Makes your melee attacks more powerful.
Add d4 to attack rolls, ability checks, and saving throws. Good luck boost.
Create an illusionary duplicate. Good for deception and positioning.

weapons.d: The cornerstone of Cleric weapons. Versatile means you can use one or two hands. Vex grants Advantage on your next attack after a hit.
Classic Cleric weapon. Simple and effective. Vex grants Advantage on your next attack after a hit.
Heavy bludgeoning damage. Slow mastery can lock down fast enemies. Good for War Clerics.
The only simple weapon with the Light property. Good for two-weapon fighting if you want to use a shield.
Heavy bludgeoning damage. Good for War Clerics who want maximum damage.
Versatile and thrown. Good for ranged attacks or melee. Vex grants Advantage on your next attack after a hit.
Your best long-range option. Slow mastery can lock down fast enemies.

armor.d: Good for a mobile Cleric who wants to avoid heavy armor. Maximizing Dexterity makes it competitive with medium armor.
Good for a Cleric who wants more AC without heavy armor. Dexterity bonus is capped at +2.
Good for a Cleric who wants more AC without heavy armor. Dexterity bonus is capped at +2.
The best armor for a frontline Cleric. No Dexterity bonus, but maximum AC.
Essential for any Cleric. +2 AC is a massive boost to your survivability.

multiclass.d: Ritual casting plus Booming Blade, True Strike, and Find Familiar. Have your familiar use Help for guaranteed Advantage on every attack.
Two more Expertise choices and a splash of spellcasting. Clean, low-investment dip.
Archery Fighting Style is a significant improvement for ranged builds. Two-Weapon Fighting is a trap — the +2–3 damage bonus is irrelevant next to Sneak Attack scaling.
One level for a Fighting Style and Divine Sense. Three levels for Lay on Hands and additional spell slots.
Bonus Action attacks can't apply Sneak Attack. Unarmored Defense (Wis-based) won't beat studded leather with high Dexterity.
Reckless Attack only works with Strength-based attacks — never good for a Wisdom Cleric. Unarmored Defense is an AC boost, but the core mechanic is wasted.
You can't deliver Sneak Attack with Eldritch Blast, and low-level Invocations aren't especially useful. If you want spellcasting, Wizard is a much easier choice.
